results.content: The K-shaped economy is increasingly evident in U.S. housing, creating a stark divide between high-end and more modest properties. By Q2 2026, the average home price of $502,700 was 22.4% higher than the median of $410,700, indicating a top-weighted market where expensive homes disproportionately influence the average. While both average and median prices have seen declines since late 2022, more modest properties are dropping faster. The median price fell 6.3% from Q3 2022 to Q2 2026, compared to a 3.5% drop in the average price over a similar period. One of them is in house prices.
